messages:
Alex: quick question — I'm prepping a release for a minor bugfix that only touches logging. should this be a patch bump (1.7.0 -> 1.7.1) or a micro (1.7.0 -> 1.7.0+micro)?
Priya: lean towards patch. customers rely on semver patches for fixes.
Jordan: +1 patch unless it's literally a docs/logging cosmetic with zero behavior change.
Casey: the tricky bit is our deploy window — if we tag a patch we trigger a longer bake window, right?
Emma: correct. patch bumps go through full canary -> 24h stability bake on prod. micro tags can go faster but no commit to changelog.
Alex: ah ok. this is logging rate limiter off by default, not user-facing. small risk.
Priya: then micro sounds ok, but add a short release note in the PR so we have an audit trail.
Jordan: also prefer micro naming to be explicit: use +micro.<reason>, e.g. v1.7.0+micro.logging-ratelimit
Casey: worried about downstream pinning. Ops teams pin patch versions, not +micro suffixes.
Alex: true — if ops pins 1.7.0 they'll miss the micro. we should document that micro is non-pinable.
Priya: propose policy: use patch bump if the change affects API/compat or requires ops pin; use +micro for internal-only, reversible, low-risk changes.
releasebot: deploybot scheduled rollout for v1.7.1 at 2026-03-22T02:00Z (canary -> 10% -> 100%).
deploybot: rollback policy: auto-rollback if 5xxs spike >1.5x baseline within 30m or error rate >2% for 10m.
Emma: can we add a label to changelog script to include +micro entries in internal release notes? currently they are filtered.
Jordan: yes — add label 'include-in-internal-notes' and release script will pick it up.
Alex: Ok let's do this: I'll change tag to v1.7.0+micro.logging-ratelimit, add PR label, and skip full patch bake. @Priya @Casey any objections?
Priya: no objections. :thumbsup:
Casey: fine with that. file a short internal note for ops about pinning caveat.
Alex: will do. thanks all.
